title: Netherstorm
body: Netherstorm was once the Plains of Farahlon, green country that a Kirin Tor mage could compare to Westfall only months ago. When Ner'zhul's portals tore Draenor apart it was left a scatter of floating islands at the edge of the Twisting Nether, and now the forces of Prince Kael'thas are finishing the ruin. From Tempest Keep, the fortress his blood elves hold, they work great manaforges that pull energy out of the sky and pipe it away underground, and the strain is tearing the land apart; one goblin scientist gives the region only months. Many have come to exploit or oppose them. The ethereal traders of the Consortium rule from the Stormspire, the Protectorate hunts a void lord and the renegade Ethereum, the goblins of Area 52 build a rocket to fly into the Nether, and the ghosts of a Kirin Tor village mourn their dead. In the north the Burning Legion builds fel reavers under the eredar Socrethar, while envoys of the Aldor and the Scryers quarrel at the Area 52 inn.

title: Area 52
body: Area 52 is a walled goblin town on the southwestern island of Netherstorm and the headquarters of B.O.O.M., the Braintrust of Orbital Operations and Mechanics. Its pride is the half-built X-52 Nether-Rocket, overseen by Rocket-Chief Fuselage. Bruisers and towering death machines keep the peace, and sappers work a fissure the goblins blasted through the middle of town, where a few workers glow suspiciously and the lead sapper insists radiation is nothing to worry about. The town is neutral ground. A Kirin Tor apprentice waits here for help, a Consortium agent hunts traitors, and envoys of the Aldor and the Scryers, newly arrived from Shattrath, argue so constantly that the innkeeper worried they would drive off trade.

title: Ruins of Enkaat
body: North of Area 52 lie the Ruins of Enkaat, an old draenei settlement fallen to rubble. Its dead have not left. Disembodied vindicators, protectors and even exarchs drift among the broken walls and attack anyone who comes near, and the goblins have taken a keen interest in the crystals they carry. The goblins of Area 52 gather etherlithium crystals here for their rocket's engine matrix, a goblin bot specialist salvages fragile draenei machines with the help of a robot called the Maxx A. Million, and the Kirin Tor apprentice Ravandwyr has heard that a crystal carried by these ghosts could mend his master's broken staff.

title: Arklon Ruins
body: Southeast of Area 52 stand the Arklon Ruins, another old draenei settlement. When Archmage Vargoth's apprentice Ravandwyr fled the attack on the Violet Tower, he sought refuge here and walked straight into the leading edge of a Burning Legion force, which wrested his master's staff from him; it ended in the hands of their leader, Ekkorash. The demons have stayed. Doomguard keep watch while artifact seekers dig for something under the dreadlord Pentatharon, and the goblin sapping crew that worked here left its machinery behind when the Legion moved in. Beyond the ruins, Farahlon giants walk the heights of Arklonis Ridge.

title: The Crumbling Waste
body: The Crumbling Waste is the broken rim of the island south of Area 52, a long ledge where the land gives way to open sky. Phase hunters drift in from the nether along its edges, nether rays and mana snappers roam the slopes, and sundered rumblers and warp aberrations haunt the southern shelf. The goblins see resources everywhere. Chief Engineer Trep sends crews to wring solid power out of the rumblers and aberrations for the X-52's engines, and Rocket-Chief Fuselage has posted a wanted notice for Netherock, king of the local mountain giants, who has been interfering with operations all along the south ledge.

title: Manaforge B'naar
body: Manaforge B'naar, west of Area 52, was the first of Kael'thas's great purple engines that the envoys from Shattrath set out to study. Its warp-masters and warp-engineers oversee the gathering of what they call warp-energy and its delivery through underground pipes to a distant destination, while geologists survey the ground and magisters and bloodwarders stand guard, with a ballista team posted outside. The magisters have refined their use of mana crystals until they can siphon great amounts of energy in seconds, attuning small bloodgem shards to the great charged crystals of the forge.

parts.body: The forge's own console betrays where it came from. B'naar was built on naaru designs, the craft of Tempest Keep bent to the prince's purposes, and it keeps the failsafe such constructs share: a permanent shutdown that can be set off at the console, given the access crystal carried by Overseer Theredis.
sources: quest 10299 description (Aldor: emergency shutdown, a safety mechanism common in naaru constructs, Theredis)
quest 10329 description (Scryers: modified naaru technology from Tempest Keep, safeguards, console and access crystal, Theredis)

parts.body: Where B'naar's four pipelines plunge into the ground, an orb attuned to warp energy took the measure of what they carry, and the Aldor did not like the readings. The energies run dangerously high, far more than this broken land can bear, and unless the forges are stopped, what little is left of Outland may be shattered to pieces.
sources: quest 10313 description and reward text

parts.body: Magistrix Larynna of the Scryers studied what the bloodgems do to those who use them. Exposure to so much raw energy greatly magnifies the blood elves' innate addiction to magic, and she was not surprised that Kael gets away with what he does: his subordinates, she says, are all but drunk on it.

title: The Heap
body: South of Area 52 lies the Heap, a junkyard of salvage that the goblins of B.O.O.M. consider their claim. The Zaxxis ethereals disagree. Once part of the Consortium, the Zaxxis broke away to go into business for themselves and have even cut deals with the Sunfury blood elves, so the Consortium's Nether-Stalker Khay'ji, who infiltrated them and attacked their leader before escaping to Area 52, wants their insignia. The goblins simply raid the ethereals' camp for its technology. Nearby sits a scrapped fel reaver, and the goblin salvager N. D. Meancamp, crouched where the Zaxxis cannot see him, is determined to have its heart.

parts.body: Khay'ji's attack did not finish the job. Word came from another of his agents among the Zaxxis that their leader, Warp-Raider Nesaad, still lives and keeps a small ethereal camp in the southwestern corner of the Heap, and Khay'ji wants him dealt with before his operation goes any further.

title: Eco-Dome Midrealm
body: Across the bridge east of Area 52, the Consortium has raised Eco-Dome Midrealm, a bubble of living green on the ruined plains. Inside, lynxes, moths and crocolisks thrive among plants that grow faster than they should, including the ivory bell, a healing herb the ethereals sell at a steep price to the Cenarion Expedition. At the Midrealm Post the trader Gahruj handles the Consortium's quarrels with the blood elves and the technician Mehrdad worries over a failing dome generator, while two goblins watch the ethereals closely: Mama Wheeler of Area 52, eager to learn their secrets, and a fellow who claims to be a simple furrier.

title: The Scrap Field
body: East of Eco-Dome Midrealm, the Burning Legion has seized a goblin salvage claim, the Scrap Field. Huge fel reaver parts litter the ground, gan'arg engineers and mo'arg doomsmiths labor among them, and their overseer Doomclaw keeps to the eastern end beneath the great pipe, driving his workers and promising to come for the little goblins. The demons never run short of hands. South of the field, at a camp they call Invasion Point: Destroyer, a warp-gate brings in a steady flow of reinforcements, and the Consortium's Drijya has slipped down there to sabotage it, pylon by pylon.

title: Manaforge Coruu
body: Manaforge Coruu stands east of Area 52 near Kirin'Var, and its arcanist boasts of having more than doubled the energy it sends to Tempest Keep. A regiment of Sunfury arcanists and researchers works here under Arcanist Ardonis, and Spellbinder Maryana keeps the Sigil of Krasus, taken from Archmage Vargoth. Arcane golems patrol the forge. It is watched all the same: Scryer spies keep a secret landing outside it, waiting for the chance to slip among Kael's followers and learn what passes between their commanders.

parts.body: Under an illusion, one of the Scryers' agents slipped into the forge and overheard Commander Dawnforge order Ardonis to send reinforcements to Manaforge Duro, which mana creatures had thrown into chaos. Ardonis protested that Coruu was badly understaffed, until an image of Pathaleon the Calculator appeared: Duro would be reinforced, for Ultris had been a complete disaster, and Prince Kael'thas would tolerate no further delays.

title: Kirin'Var Village
body: Kirin'Var Village was built by the Kirin Tor mages of the Alliance expedition once they knew they were trapped in Outland, and by the custodian's count it held for twenty years against countless orc assaults. It did not survive Kael'thas. His forces leveled the town in an assault that began with a thundering noise and a blinding flash, and ever since, beings of pure mana have streamed into the ruins of Wizard Row. Now the dead keep the village. Ghostly apprentices haunt the Town Square, a maddened spectral smith lingers in his old workshop, tormented souls wander the Chapel Yard, and an old farmer pines for his lost cow. By the lieutenant-sorcerer's account, only two spirits remember who they were.

parts.body: A fragment recovered from the ruins told Lieutenant-Sorcerer Morran what had opened the attack: a mana bomb, a weapon he thought even the best minds of Dalaran could never have conceived. The sheer force of its blast tore a rift in the nether, and through it the mana creatures reach the village.

title: The Violet Tower
body: At the heart of Kirin'Var rises the Violet Tower, sanctuary and prison to Archmage Vargoth. When Kael'thas took the village he stripped the archmage of his possessions and sealed the tower with a curse that no member of the Kirin Tor may cross in either direction, so that Vargoth's own people cannot reach him. An arcane golem named Ar'kelos guards the base and smothers the archmage's magic, and the ward keeps Vargoth from scrying out the force that holds it in place. Kael'thas was always a talented mage, the archmage admits, but he had never seen power like the prince wielded in the attack.

parts.body: The tower's defenses did not fall to force alone. Naberius, another of Vargoth's apprentices, was an ardent student drawn to necromancy, and when Kael'thas appeared with his forces he seized the chance to betray his master, handing the blood elves the secrets of the tower's defenses.
sources: quest 10319 description (Naberius handed over the secrets to the tower's defense)

parts.body: The force behind the ward was found at last, by scrying with one of the giant Apex's crystals as a focus. It led to Commander Sarannis, an advisor of the prince and no mage at all, whom Vargoth remembers from the day the village fell. She does not sustain the curse; she keeps its key, far off in Tempest Keep, and until it is destroyed the tower stays sealed.

title: Sunfury Hold
body: North of the Violet Tower lies Sunfury Hold, the camp to which Kael'thas's forces withdrew after destroying Kirin'Var. The village's ghostly custodian says the very soldiers who killed them toast their amazing victory here, among the tents and ballistae, the archers and flamekeepers. Its commander, Spellreaver Marathelle, carried off the heliotrope oculus that unlocks Krasus's Compendium during the attack, no doubt taking it for a pretty bauble. Custodian Dieworth wants the garrison slain, and Lieutenant-Sorcerer Morran wants every tent and siege engine burned to ash, so that Kael's zealous followers have nothing to return to.

title: Manaforge Duro
body: Manaforge Duro, east of Eco-Dome Midrealm, is the forge slipping out of its masters' hands. Its rising output has drawn swarms of errant mana creatures, the Sunfury garrison is losing control, and the Aldor fear that an explosion here could set off a chain reaction across Outland. Its defenders include notorious names. Master Daellis Dawnstrike, the crimson-armored archer who led the attack on Kirin'Var, has been sent here to restore order, and Summoner Kanthin keeps Archmage Vargoth's familiar, Glacius, as a trophy. The blood elves also hold a shipment of Consortium surveying equipment they never paid for, and west of the forge roams Apex, a giant that bears great crystals.

title: Cosmowrench
body: Cosmowrench is a small goblin outpost in the Vortex Fields at the far eastern edge of Netherstorm, close beneath Tempest Keep, a miniature Area 52 with its own bruisers, a weapon merchant and a flight master. Its most curious resident is a human named Sab'aoth, who once amused himself by accepting any challenge offered and now runs a reagent and poison business while writing a book about his time with the Twilight's Hammer. One of his best sellers is the caustic blood of the warp chasers that swarm the Vortex Fields, which only his foul-mouthed imp, Zeppit, can gather safely.

title: Tempest Keep
body: Beyond the Tempest Rift at Netherstorm's eastern edge, the fortress of Tempest Keep hangs apart from the land. Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider made it his seat, and it is the reason the manaforges exist: their energy flows to it, and the Aldor reckon that once the last forge falls, the prince will be left to drain whatever reserves he has stored. Its satellites are the Mechanar, the Botanica, the Arcatraz and the Eye. From Shattrath City, the naaru A'dal sends champions to break into its satellites and to bring the prince to account.

title: The Stormspire
body: The Stormspire is the seat of the Consortium in Netherstorm, a towering spire reached by an elevator from its base and flanked by the eco-domes Skyperch and Sutheron, where talbuks and lashers thrive under the ethereals' shields. At its summit, Nexus-Prince Haramad receives visitors as a holographic image, a precaution against his many enemies. Below, dealers sell everything from exotic weapons to rare creatures, Head Engineer Ghabar tends the dome generators, a transmuter whose skill is known in a thousand worlds takes on alchemists, and a Cenarion Expedition envoy bargains for the domes' secrets. Nexus-guards and alarm bots watch for trouble.

title: Manaforge Ara
body: Manaforge Ara, on its own island in the northwest, is the last and best defended of the working forges, and it holds the secret the others only hinted at. Demons labor openly beside the Sunfury here: mo'arg warp-masters and gan'arg tinkers tend the machinery, a doomguard overmaster rules the Trelleum Mine beneath it, and its overseer bears the strangely un-elven name of Azarad. Not every elf is loyal: a Sunfury magister stationed here has offered to defect. Across the bridge at Tuluman's Landing, a Consortium agent poses as a weapon seller, and the young Aldor Kaylaan waits, sole survivor of the ten who went in.

parts.body: Another doubter works in the mine below. Foreman Sundown, demoted from his post, has come to see the pilgrimage from Quel'Thalas to Outland as a lie Kael'thas told to strengthen his forces in Netherstorm, and he has tried in vain to persuade his brethren to leave, all the more with the Burning Legion here.

Forge Base: Gehenna is the staging ground for the Legion's army, where most of its teleporters stand, wrathbringers gather by the regiment, and mo'arg keep the gates in repair under the demon Silroth. Legion fel cannons guard both. Morug and Silroth each carry half of the stone that opens Socrethar's teleporters, and close by lies Invasion Point: Overlord, the doorway to Socrethar's own island.

title: Socrethar's Seat
body: Socrethar's Seat is a craggy island off the northwestern corner of Netherstorm, from which the eredar Socrethar directs the Burning Legion's campaign. No road reaches it. Only his most trusted lieutenants may pass, by a Legion teleporter that answers only to his stone, and wrath lords and hatecryers keep watch over the crags. It is here that champions of the Aldor and the Scryers come at last to face him, each backed by the power of a leader in Shattrath.

title: Netherstone
body: The Netherstone is a crystal landmark in the north of Netherstorm that no one saw when this was a lush, green land; its formations were exposed only recently. They yield a mineral the Consortium calls farahlite, after the land's old name, and the purest grade grows on the backs of the Farahlon giants who roam here under their patriarch, Cragskaar. Beyond it to the northeast lies Eco-Dome Farfield, a remote dome few ethereals visit, where scythetooth raptors nest and an ethereal technician tests repairs to the dome generators.

parts.body: Its remoteness has made it a hiding place. The raptor nests of Farfield hold more than eggs: pieces of the ethereals' own dome generators, taken by two goblins of Area 52 who pass for hunters at the Stormspire and slip out here to stash them.

title: Ruins of Farahlon
body: High in the north of Netherstorm stand the Ruins of Farahlon, where old draenei banners still mark the stones, and which the Consortium's Zephyrion means to excavate. The Burning Legion moved in first, a few weeks ago. Then one of its dreadlords, Culuthas, killed off all the other demons and summoned hounds and eyes of his own to serve him. He has held the ruins as his own ever since, and an image of Socrethar, the Legion's master in Netherstorm, hovers close beside him.

parts.body: The prize at the top of the ruins is the ata'mal crystal, an artifact out of draenei legend whose bearer, it is said, gains the powers of a god. The Consortium tracked it here by triangulation and found it already in the Legion's grip, for the crystal was moving.

title: The Protectorate Watch Post
body: On the island east of the Stormspire, the ethereal Protectorate keeps its Watch Post under Commander Ameer. Its soldiers fight on two fronts: against the void lord Dimensius at the ruined Manaforge Ultris, and against the Ethereum, whose Staging Grounds lie directly to the south. There the Ethereum drill behind their perimeter defenses under Captain Zovax, readying for something the commander fears may be a strike on Ultris, and a Protectorate platoon that marched toward them ten days ago has sent no word since. At the post a researcher studies the pollution draining from Ultris, a flesh handler keeps subservient flesh beasts, and a nether drake waits to carry volunteers into battle.

parts.body: The silence from the south was broken when the platoon's captain, Tyralius, was freed from an Ethereum cell, gravely hurt but expected to live. His word turned the post's attention south again: the Staging Grounds hide whole fields of prisons, holding beings taken from every corner of the universe, and the Consortium means to find a way through their locks.

parts.body: For the Protectorate the discovery made its whole reason for being plain. Behind their defenses the Ethereum draw on the void energies of the ruined forge to remake themselves as nexus-stalkers. They are not hunting the void lord at all; they mean to become void.

The blood elves lost both the forge and the mine beneath it. Voidwraiths drift through the ruin, seeping sludge fills the surrounding pools, and in Access Shaft Zeon on its south side lie corpses drained by another void lord, Arconus, which hide flesh beasts waiting to burst out. The Ethereum patrol the Voidwind Plateau around it with nullifiers and jailors, while two Protectorate agents, split up in a firefight, hold out at the mine.

title: Celestial Ridge
body: East of Manaforge Ultris, the Celestial Ridge is a forest of arcane crystals where nether dragons nest in every stage of growth, from eggs to full-grown dragons under a leader named Veraku. They hatch and mature quickly, drawing on the strange energies that forged their kind in the destruction of Draenor. Such creatures attract both profiteers and scholars. The ethereal Wind Trader Marid, who keeps a teleport pad on the ridge, wants their essence for a client he would rather not name, while two quiet watchers at the north end of the ridge, Tyri and her companion Jorad Mace, hope to understand them before others rush to exploit them.

parts.body: When the first essence was gathered, a shrouded figure appeared at the pad, the projection of someone keeping watch from hiding. It named Marid's buyers: the ethereal meant to sell the essence to the blood elves like so much candy. Marid, the figure warned, was a swindler wearing an honest trader's face.

He hires newcomers on the spot as Junior Technician 3rd Grade, promises promotion as fast as they bring him parts, and despairs aloud that his crew is at T-minus never. When a netherologist's report warned that the storm would rip the region apart within months, his only complaint was that the timetable would have to move up.

title: Archmage Vargoth
body: Archmage Vargoth led the Kirin Tor contingent of the Alliance expedition, and when it became clear they were trapped in Outland he took his mages to the Plains of Farahlon and founded Kirin'Var Village. The Kirin Tor had entrusted him with two treasures of Krasus, a powerful sigil and the spellbook holding every spell Krasus mastered, both of them boons in the war against the orcs. When Kael'thas attacked, Vargoth gave his staff to his apprentice Ravandwyr and bade him flee, then was stripped of his possessions and sealed in the Violet Tower. He speaks to outsiders through an image the staff conjures, still wondering how fields that once looked like Westfall were ruined in mere months.

parts.body: His freedom came with the keystone, brought out of Tempest Keep to the tower to be destroyed. Vargoth met it with amazement and some unease: from the little he had seen of what Farahlon had become, he doubted he wanted to go outside at all, but anything was better than living out his life a prisoner.

title: Custodian Dieworth
body: Custodian Dieworth administered Kirin'Var Village on Archmage Vargoth's behalf, and he still does, though he died in the attack with nearly everyone else. Unlike most of the village dead, he kept his memory and identity. He mourns colleagues whose spirits wander in mindless anger, tries to free a few by returning their treasured belongings to their homes, and has never forgotten the crimson-armored archer who led the assault. Bitter toward a prince who once called himself a member of the Kirin Tor, he hungers for vengeance on the Sunfury who toast their victory at Sunfury Hold.

parts.body: When the archer, Master Daellis Dawnstrike, was dead at last, the custodian seemed close to tears. It was through, he said, and if he could will himself out of existence he would, but the truth is that he does not know how to let go; that, he supposes, is the price of keeping such strong ties to this place.

title: Commander Ameer
body: Commander Ameer leads the ethereal Protectorate in Netherstorm and addresses everyone else as fleshling. He tells the ethereals' story plainly. The Ethereum were the ruling class of his homeworld, K'aresh, which his people fled shortly before the void lord Dimensius ravaged it; they vowed vengeance and have hunted him ever since, but vengeance has twisted them, and several nexus-princes broke away to found new factions, the Consortium among them. The Protectorate, he insists, was born as a reaction to the Ethereum, not to Dimensius, and he holds them just as dangerous. He works through transponders and projected images.

parts.body: Ameer set about cataloguing the prisoner tags found in Ethereum territory and in time cracked their code. The back of each tag records where its prisoner is held and what kind of prisoner it is, and the front always bears the same phrase, A Thousand Worlds. He does not know its meaning, but to him it sounds insidious.

title: Tyri
body: Tyri keeps watch over the nether dragons of the Celestial Ridge from its north end with her companion, Jorad Mace, and the pair take pains not to reveal themselves. She reaches newcomers first through a projection of her current form, urging them to have nothing more to do with Wind Trader Marid, whom she counts a swindler posing as a merchant, and to work with her instead. She has never seen anything like these dragons: they seem to have inherited their sire's temperament, yet they have become something entirely different.

parts.body: Tyri is properly Tyrygosa, of the brood of Malygos: a blue dragon. Word of the strange dragonkin on the ridge has traveled far, and she fears that many will rush to exploit them for profit without understanding what they are, so she and Jorad mean to gain insight into the creatures before others discover them.

parts.body: She came on rumors of a new breed, perhaps even descendants of Deathwing, and found dragons with all the black flight's ferocity and its hatred of her own, yet entirely alien. Hoping their powers might serve her flight, she had their leader, Veraku, defeated, and now means to win them over with time and a firm show of authority, keeping them from falling under the sway of a malevolent power.

title: Socrethar
body: Socrethar is the eredar who commands the Burning Legion in Netherstorm. His seat is an island of crags off the land's northwestern corner, cut off from every road: the only way across is a Legion teleporter that answers to his own stone, and his demons guard the heights. Those who come against him face a foe of terrible power, who answers blades with cleaving blows and wards himself against magic while shadow bolts and barrages of fire rain down on his enemies.

parts.body: Among the draenei his name is infamous, enough to make most of them shudder, and from that island he gives his orders where none but his most trusted servants may follow. The Aldor hold that his demons are the only reason Kael'thas could ever make use of the technology of Tempest Keep.

title: Dimensius the All-Devouring
body: Dimensius the All-Devouring is a void lord who came into Netherstorm through a tear in the nether atop Manaforge Ultris and has made the ruined forge his own. Void creatures go out from him to ravage the island around it, and he proclaims, in a voice that carries far, that time has meaning only to mortals: he is infinite, and in time all will be devoured. The ethereals of the Protectorate are his sworn foes, and their avengers under Captain Saeed stand ready to march on Ultris.

parts.body: The tear is the source of his safety. It binds him to the void and keeps him phased out of this world, beyond the reach of physical harm. Professor Dabiri of the Protectorate means to lock onto that conduit and destroy it, then destroy Dimensius, beginning with fragments taken from the void creatures he sends out.

parts.body: The ethereals have cause to hate him. By Commander Ameer's account, Dimensius unleashed his void armies on their homeworld of K'aresh shortly after the ethereals fled it and laid waste to all that stood in his way, and the Ethereum have hunted him ever since, sworn to vengeance.

title: The X-52 Nether-Rocket
body: On the bridge into Netherstorm, Netherologist Coppernickels studies the ethereal currents and sends newcomers on to Area 52 with his overdue notes, which warn that the nether energies will rip the region apart within months. Rocket-Chief Fuselage simply moves up his timetable. Each new hire becomes a Junior Technician, sent to the Ruins of Enkaat for etherlithium crystals for the engine matrix, while a bot specialist sends a robot to salvage draenei machines. Chief Engineer Trep, who only took the post because the security jobs were gone, still lacks an engine core and hopes mana wraith essence will jump-start the engines. Boots the bartender brews rocket fuel from shale oil and nether ray venom, and the sappers zap their abandoned gear back from the Arklon Ruins.

parts.body: The essence was not enough. Trep's next idea was an extractor built by Xyrol, which turns the power of the sundered rumblers and warp aberrations on the Crumbling Waste into something solid enough to gather and pour into the engines.

body: Papa Wheeler of B.O.O.M. decides that the ethereals scavenging the Heap deserve to be robbed in turn, then sends help against the demons who have seized the Scrap Field. His wife, Mama Wheeler, who works among the ethereals at the Midrealm Post and is not pleased to hear herself called his partner, wants the small fel reaver parts the Legion leaves lying about, and then decides that killing the overseer Doomclaw might scare the demons away. Everyone agrees the Legion is creeping closer, moving in on the goblins' claims one at a time.

title: The Curse of the Violet Tower
body: In Area 52 the Kirin Tor apprentice Ravandwyr seeks help for his master, Archmage Vargoth, imprisoned in the cursed Violet Tower where no member of the Kirin Tor may pass. Vargoth gave him his staff and bade him flee the attack, but he sought refuge at the Arklon Ruins, walked straight into a Burning Legion force and lost the staff to the demons; their leader, Ekkorash, holds it now. Ravandwyr is ashamed of his failure, and his master knows nothing of it. He will not rest until the staff is restored to the archmage.

parts.body: The staff came back broken, its crystalline headpiece taken, and Ravandwyr reshaped it around a crystal carried by the ghosts of Enkaat. Its magic can pierce the tower's defenses only in hands outside the Kirin Tor, and through it the archmage's image appears. The curse can be broken, he says, but not without help, and the first thing he needs is the Sigil of Krasus, which Spellbinder Maryana keeps at Manaforge Coruu.

Then the golem Ar'kelos fell, and its dampening field with it, yet the curse held. A crystal from the giant Apex served as a scrying focus, and the trail led to Commander Sarannis in Tempest Keep's Botanica.

title: The Ghosts of Kirin'Var
body: Custodian Dieworth and Lieutenant-Sorcerer Morran are the only spirits in Kirin'Var who still know themselves. Dieworth sets out to quiet the angry dead and to lay a few to rest by returning their treasures: a battle-mage's sword, an heirloom storybook, a high elven cloak and a gnome's beloved hat. Morran wants to learn what weapon Kael'thas used, for the attack began with a thundering flash and mana creatures have streamed into the village ever since. Dieworth's thoughts turn to vengeance as well, on the soldiers who toast their victory at Sunfury Hold and on Master Daellis Dawnstrike, who led the attack and now serves at Manaforge Duro.

parts.body: A fragment showed it was a mana bomb, whose blast tore open the nether. Seeing the blood elves fight the same mana creatures with defenses fueled by concentrated energy, Morran had their energy sources captured, and with them he set out to ring the village with runes that would hold the creatures back.

title: Shutting Down the Manaforges
body: A'dal sent the Aldor and the Scryers to Netherstorm to learn what Kael'thas is doing with his manaforges, and since they reached the Area 52 inn they have not stopped arguing. Spymaster Thalodien prefers assassinating Kael's specialists, Exarch Orelis would rather make calculated attacks and gather what can be learned, and the Aldor agree to raid Manaforge B'naar only so that the Scryers will keep gathering information. Each side does its part. The Scryers go after the personnel roster carried by a ballista captain outside B'naar, while the Aldor thin out the magisters and bloodwarders who guard it. What the great purple forges are for, and how far their power reaches, is what both orders mean to find out.

parts.body: One of the first things the Scryers learned came from the forge's own magisters. Magistrix Larynna tried the bloodgem shards they use to siphon energy and found that the rush feeds the blood elves' hunger for magic far beyond its natural measure, enough to explain, she thought, why Kael's followers let him get away with so much.
sources: quest 10204 description and reward text

parts.body: The roster gave the Scryers their targets among Kael's specialists, and the forge itself gave up a greater secret. The manaforges are naaru craft, modified from the technology of Tempest Keep, and like most naaru constructs they carry a safeguard: an emergency shutdown, begun at each forge's console with an access crystal kept by its overseer.

parts.body: One by one the forges went dark: B'naar, then Coruu, then Duro, where swarms of mana creatures had thrown the garrison into chaos, and at last Ara, the most heavily defended of all. Kael'thas had lost the last of his working forges. Yet at Ara the shutdown uncovered something worse: the Burning Legion, allied with Kael'thas Sunstrider, and word of it would soon reach Shattrath.

title: A Pact with the Legion
body: How did Kael'thas master naaru technology so quickly? It should have taken him years even to begin to understand it, and his disciplined army destroys its written orders. The Aldor seize Sunfury briefings from embattled Manaforge Duro that point to outside help in building and running the forges, and follow the trail to Tuluman's Landing, where the young Kaylaan is the only survivor of ten who went into Manaforge Ara. The Scryers hear from a Sunfury magister stationed at Ara who wishes to defect and swears he has the information they need. Both trails lead into Ara.

parts.body: The answer was the Burning Legion. At Manaforge Ara its servants labor beside the Sunfury, and the truth can no longer be hidden: Kael'thas Sunstrider has allied himself with the Legion, and his army and the demons now serve under the same banner.

Both orders took the halves of his teleportation stone from Forgemaster Morug at Forge Base: Oblivion and from Silroth at Forge Base: Gehenna, and with the stone whole, the way to his seat lay open to whoever had the strength to go.

He fought the Lightwarden who had trained him until Ishanah came and offered herself in his place. Socrethar struck her down, and Kaylaan broke free, called on the Light and raised her, then fell to Socrethar's magic before the eredar died. Not even Ishanah's prayers could bring him back.

title: The Ata'mal Crystal
body: The Aldor and the Scryers both send newcomers to aid the Consortium's Nether-Stalker Khay'ji, hoping to bring the ethereals around to the naaru's way of seeing things now that the Consortium's dealings with the blood elves have soured. Khay'ji has been tasked by Nexus-Prince Haramad with recovering a crystal artifact from the Arklon Ruins, where the Burning Legion has moved in to dig for itself, and the crystal is in the hands of the dreadlord Pentatharon. What the prince truly wants, Khay'ji cannot say for certain.

parts.body: Pentatharon's crystal proved to be nothing special, but the Legion was plainly searching for something in particular, and Khay'ji hoped it was not the crystal the nexus-prince wanted so badly. Meanwhile he settled scores with the Zaxxis traitors at the Heap, ethereals who had broken with the Consortium to deal with the Sunfury.

Recovered, the equipment went to Haramad at the Stormspire, and he revealed his true aim: a crystal from draenei legend, said to bestow godlike powers on its bearer and in danger of being unearthed by the Legion. The equipment would find it by triangulation.

title: The Ethereum
body: Commander Ameer suspects that the Ethereum at the Staging Grounds south of his Watch Post are preparing for something, perhaps an assault on Ultris, so volunteers are sent to break through their perimeter, topple Captain Zovax and report through a captured transponder. Other threads lead the same way. Five Consortium dealers have gone missing in two days, and the Consortium suspects the Ethereum. Captain Tyralius took a Protectorate platoon south ten days ago and has not been heard from since, though a faint reading may be a distress signal. And a prison orb salvaged from Ethereum territory seems to hold one of the Protectorate's own.

parts.body: The Ethereum hide their plans well. Their data cells hold nothing, and only someone who drinks an Ethereum essence, at real risk to the mind, can see the relays that carry their secrets. What the relays hold is worse than an assault: the Ethereum are not hunting Dimensius but becoming void, using the ruined manaforge's void energy to bond themselves into nexus-stalkers.

parts.body: Ameer struck at the transformation through the manaforge energy tube the Ethereum use as a conduit, and a holographic demolitionist overloaded it. Then the force fields around Nexus-King Salhadaar were brought down, and Salhadaar, who had waged his crusade against all who stood in his way for a thousand years or more, was destroyed.

parts.body: A captured Protectorate soldier was found alive in the Staging Grounds and brought home to the Watch Post. His platoon had been ambushed on the island's upper ledges by ethereals who looked like Ethereum but wore wrappings of the void, and only Captain Tyralius had been spared, likely for a cell. Ameer judged the soldier might be the key to the whole Ethereum operation.

parts.body: Captain Tyralius was found alive in an Ethereum prison, badly wounded. He spoke of fields of prisons like the one that held him, full of creatures from all across the universe, and the Consortium began working on ways to break the Ethereum's locks.

parts.body: From the prisoners' tags Ameer broke the Ethereum's code and combined their prison keys into a tablet that read: a thousand worlds shattered, a thousand more to overcome, by the will of the Nexus-King. On its back was a name, the stasis chambers of Bash'ir, and the trail led on to Bash'ir's Landing in Blade's Edge.

title: The Eco-Dome Thieves
body: The Consortium brings its eco-domes wherever it goes, but in Netherstorm the generators are failing. At Eco-Dome Midrealm the technician Mehrdad finds generator pieces at the bottom of a lake where crocolisks have taken an interest in them, and sends word to Head Engineer Ghabar at the Stormspire, who orders diagnostics of the main generator in Eco-Dome Sutheron. Others have their own interest in the domes. At the Stormspire, Aurine Moonblaze of the Cenarion Expedition prepares to negotiate with the ethereals for their technology and studies its effects on the life inside, while at the Midrealm Post a goblin who calls himself a simple furrier buys pelts.

parts.body: Ghabar's readings matched Mehrdad's exactly: equipment had failed or gone missing. A prototype repair kit, tested by Tashar at distant Eco-Dome Farfield, worked, but Tashar saw the pattern in the damage. Key pieces of generator units were missing from a number of sites. This was no accident: the Consortium was being stolen from, and Ghabar began to think of locking down the Stormspire.

parts.body: The furrier is nothing of the kind. Shauly Pore was sent from Area 52 to appraise the technology the ethereals use to generate their domes, and he poses as a simple furrier because the ethereals are clever and observant. His masters prefer agents who are not goblins wherever they can find them.
sources: quest 10433 description

parts.body: His associates at the Stormspire, Action Jaxon and Audi the Needle, pose as hunters. Out in the field they have been collecting pieces of the domes' generators and hiding them in the raptor nests of Eco-Dome Farfield, enough for Area 52's own needs with spares to sell to the Cenarion Expedition at a profit.

parts.body: Aurine's tests showed both promise and danger. Focused on the lashers, the domes' energies accelerated growth until it bred extreme aggression, and talbuks tagged under the dome are watched to see if they mature as fast. With proper control, she believes, such technology could regrow the ruined lands of Outland and Azeroth.

title: Kalynna Lathred
body: Kalynna Lathred is a mage who keeps to Area 52 and reads the stars, which she says foretold the arrival of the messenger Archmage Alturus sent her from Karazhan. She left the Kirin Tor in pursuit of knowledge her order forbade, and finds it beyond ironic that she is now asked to help them with that very knowledge. Alturus's request is no small one: he wants to raise a whole dragon, the dead blue Arcanagos, back from his charred remains. Her help has a price. First she wants two tomes she has long sought: the Tome of Dusk, owned by the orc warlock Nethekurse, and the Book of Forgotten Names, kept by the arakkoa Darkweaver Syth.

parts.body: With the tomes delivered, Kalynna kept her end of the bargain and bound her helper's essence to that of the dead dragon. An urn's energy, released on the Master's Terrace in Karazhan, would bring life back to the charred remains of Arcanagos; the creature must then be defeated and its essence carried to Alturus at once. Should that fail, the stars warned, a great terror would be loosed upon the skies, a terror known as Nightbane.
